page: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture. The instance runs on Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. It features 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapping directly to 4 vCPUs. The hardware includes a 64 KB L1 data cache, a 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware cryptographic acceleration enabled via AES instructions. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio, alongside 161 GB of local SSD temporary storage.

Benchmark evaluation shows balanced standard compute performance but modest throughput under intensive instruction sets. In stress-ng testing, the instance records average tier results for both single-core (1822.68) and multi-core (7252.56) operations. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 48.18 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieves 27.09 GB/sec, placing memory operations in the middle percentile tier. Single-threaded gzip compression performs well at 24.09 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations reach an average ranking of 2892.68.

Performance tradeoffs manifest in computational workloads requiring heavy vectorization or complex decompression. The Neoverse-N1 design lacks AVX and AMX instruction extensions, resulting in lower scores on Geekbench 6 (1056 single-core, 3519 multi-core) and PassMark encryption tests (649.7). Redis write throughput records 4.99 million operations per second, while small-model LLM inference generation registers 41.41 tokens per second.

Azure E4pds_v5 offers favorable resource density for memory-bound applications that do not require x86 instruction compatibility. The inclusion of bundled 161 GB NVMe-class local SSD storage complements the 32 GB RAM allocation. It is appropriate for relational databases, Redis caching layers, middleware runtime environments, web backends, and moderate data manipulation tasks running natively on Linux ARM environments.
description: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 3.0 GHz, 32.0 GB of memory, and 161 GB of local SSD storage. Designed with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio on an arm64 architecture, it delivers steady compute across general multi-threaded processes, achieving average tier results in stress-ng tests and uncached memory bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate lower throughput in encryption, vector processing, and LLM token generation due to the absence of x86 vector extensions. With local scratch storage and dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores, the instance serves as a cost-efficient platform for ARM-compatible database servers, in-memory caches, middleware, and standard backend application services.
